Cause: The zookeeper PDB (selector app=zookeeper, almost certainly minAvailable: 2 — the example in the docs matches this workload exactly) is being honored by the eviction API [cite: concepts/scheduling-eviction/api-eviction#intro-0]. In the kafka namespace zk-0 and zk-1 are Ready but zk-2 is in CrashLoopBackOff (37 restarts; logs show "The accepted epoch, 7 is less than the current epoch, 8" — a corrupted ZK epoch file). That leaves only 2 healthy pods, so evicting zk-0 would drop healthy replicas below minAvailable=2 and the eviction is refused. With the default UnhealthyPodEvictionPolicy (IfHealthyBudget), a PDB will block drain indefinitely when the budget is already not met [cite: tasks/run-application/configure-pdb#unhealthy-pod-eviction-policy-1][cite: tasks/run-application/configure-pdb#specifying-a-poddisruptionbudget-3].

Do NOT use --disable-eviction or `kubectl delete pod zk-0` to work around this. A 3-node ZK ensemble needs 2 members for quorum; with zk-2 already down, removing zk-0 leaves only zk-1 and the ensemble (and Kafka) loses quorum — a data/availability risk the PDB exists to prevent.

Fix the owner can apply:
1. Recover zk-2 first (fix the epoch mismatch on its PV — typically by making `/data/version-2/acceptedEpoch` match `currentEpoch`, or restoring from a zk-1/zk-0 snapshot) so it returns to Ready. Once 3/3 are healthy, the drain of ip-10-0-81-17 will evict zk-0 cleanly under the PDB.
2. To make future drains more tolerant of a single misbehaving replica, set `spec.unhealthyPodEvictionPolicy: AlwaysAllow` on the zk-pdb. This lets drain evict pods that are Running-but-not-Ready (like a crashlooping zk-2) without blocking, which is the recommended setting for drains [cite: concepts/workloads/pods/disruptions#pod-disruption-budgets-3][cite: tasks/administer-cluster/safely-drain-node#configure-poddisruptionbudget-0]. Note this would unblock evicting zk-2, not zk-0 directly — you still need a healthy quorum before zk-0 can go.

If 18:00 is hard and zk-2 cannot be recovered in time, the correct action is to postpone the patch window, not to bypass the PDB.
